newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Nicaragua denounces China's threats over Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua denounces China's threats over Taiwan.

text.p: Nicaragua's U.N. envoy on Tuesday sharply denounced threats by China against his country for supporting U.N. membership for Taiwan.
"Nicaragua denounces before world public opinion the threat of which it has been the object," Nicaraguan U.N. ambassador Enrique Paguaga Fernandez told a news conference.
Nicaragua reserved the right to "make use of the highest and most effective means of petitioning" international bodies if the threats against it materialised.

He was referring to a recent letter from Chinese U.N. envoy Qin Huasun to Secretary-General Kofi Annan condemning "Nicaragua and a very small number of other countries" for proposing that the General Assembly session opening in September discuss granting Taiwan U.N. membership.
This is the fifth consecutive year that such a proposal has been made. It has been blocked each time in the Assembly's steering committee, failing to win inscription on the agenda.

This year's move was sponsored by nine countries, compared with 16 last year, reflecting efforts by China to wean away the mostly Central American, Caribbean and African nations that have relations with Taiwan.

Qin said in his letter that if Nicaragua and the other sponsors of the move "continue to isolate themselves and stand against the overwhelming majority of member states, they would ultimately pay the price for it."

Beijing took over China's U.N. seat in 1971 when Taiwan, to which the Nationalist Chinese government retreated in 1949, was expelled from the United Nations. China regards the island as a renegade province and reacts fiercely to any move to recognise or seat Taiwan.
Nicaraguan President Arnoldo Aleman is due to visit Taiwan in early August.

"We don't have to ask permission from anyone in order to take our own position," said Paguaga, who was accompanied by the chairman of the Nicaraguan Nation Assembly's foreign affairs committee, Adolfo Calero. "We are a sovereign, independent nation. We don't follow instructions from any foreign power."

The Nicaraguan government, "unquestionably a product of popular elections," had been threatened by one that made "ample use of torture and other malicious treatment...and of mass summary executions," he said, quoting from a report by the human rights organisation Amnesty International.

Asked later about China's charge that Taiwan won support through "dollar diplomacy" in the form of aid and trade, Paguaga said Beijing's U.N. envoy recently offered to establish diplomatic relations with Nicaragua and compensate it for any loss of aid if it would break ties with Taiwan.
"I told him our policy was to continue good relations with Taiwan," Paguaga said.
